ai.title: Add Knowledge Files documentation
ai.summary: New `knowledge-files.mdx` documents usage of `knowledge.md` files for storing project context, best practices, and post-change verification commands. Updated `where-codebuff-shines.mdx` clarifies the file pattern and removes redundant task tips. Scope limited to web content tips.

eli5.text: If you look at the tips section of the website, you'll now see a new page called 'Knowledge Files' that explains how to create and organize plain-text files (named knowledge.md) to store important project context like coding standards, architecture decisions, and best practices. The existing guidance about where the assistant works best has also been updated to clearly mention these knowledge files, removing some redundant tips. This helps you understand and use this feature effectively.

ai.title: Add interactive terminal demo and PostHog analytics
ai.summary: Landing page now features an interactive terminal demo backed by a new `/api/demo` route using DeepSeek. PostHog analytics integrated for web traffic, requiring user consent via `CookieConsentCard`. Scope covers `web` package, including new components, API routes, and provider setup.

eli5.text: Visitors to the landing page can now play with a simulated coding terminal right in their browser, typing example commands and seeing responses, backed by an AI assistant model running live through a new web endpoint. While there, the site asks for permission before tracking how people move around with PostHog analytics, and only starts collecting that data after you agree, respecting privacy settings like Do Not Track. If someone looked closely, they'd see a new consent banner and notice the terminal demo has built-in limits to prevent abuse, like a cap on how often one IP address can send requests.

ai.title: Fix InteractiveTerminalDemo state race and API origin validation
ai.summary: Refactored `handleInput` in `InteractiveTerminalDemo.tsx` to use functional `setTerminalLines` updates instead of mutating a local copy, preventing race conditions with mutation handlers. Updated `api/demo/route.ts` to parse and normalize origin URLs (stripping `www.`, comparing host/port) rather than strict string equality, while enforcing CORS headers on all error responses. Scope includes web components, demo API route, and knowledge base docs.

eli5.text: If you typed commands into the interactive demo terminal (like 'help' or a rainbow request), the text now appears steadily instead of occasionally blinking in the wrong spot or getting dropped when several commands landed at once. Behind the scenes, the origin check on the demo API now treats 'www.example.com' and 'example.com' as the same site, so visitors on either version won't be unexpectedly blocked. The change is live today for anyone using the public demo.

ai.title: Add scraped content to knowledge files
ai.summary: New `addScrapedContentToFiles` function parses URLs from knowledge file content and appends scraped blocks. `getProjectFileContext` now uses this enriched content instead of raw files. Affects `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now pull in extra background information from web pages while it reads project files, so answers can include details that were previously only linked but not actually brought into the project's knowledge files. This only applies when a knowledge file already contains a web address; the assistant fetches that page and adds a condensed version of it to the file's content on the fly. You would notice this if you were looking at how the assistant works internally behind the scenes: instead of only seeing the raw text you wrote, the system now also sees appended summaries scraped from those links. It is live today, but only affects the internal knowledge-reading process and not anything you directly see.

ai.title: Bump codebuff to 1.0.134
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.134 in `npm-app/package.json`. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: If you use the AI dev assistant, updating to this version lets you see a new interactive terminal demo right on the landing page, and the assistant can now pull in content from URLs you provide and add it directly to its knowledge files. Behind the scenes, it also fixes a timing bug that could glitch the demo when you type quickly, and it tightens up how the app checks where requests come from. This version went live on January 9, 2025.

ai.title: Enforce relative paths in readfiles
ai.summary: System prompt clarifies that `read_files` paths must be relative to the project root, explicitly warning against absolute paths. `getFiles` in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` adds an `isAbsolute` check to reject absolute paths before resolving them against the project root. This prevents path traversal issues and ensures consistent relative path handling across the agent.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to open files, it now refuses any file path that starts from the root of your computer (like /Users/name/project/file.txt) and only accepts paths measured from your project folder (like src/components/button.txt). If it ever sees a full system path, it blocks the attempt and reports the file is outside your project, preventing the assistant from accidentally reading sensitive files elsewhere on your machine. This protection is active today.

ai.title: Replace bun-types with @types/bun
ai.summary: Switched from `bun-types` to `@types/bun` across all packages. Updated `package.json` devDependencies and `tsconfig.json` types arrays in backend, scripts, test, and root. This aligns with Bun's official type definitions.

eli5.text: The development team swapped out an older set of helper instructions (bun-types) for the official, up-to-date ones (@types/bun) that the tool makers now provide. This affects only the software's internal build process, so you won't see any visible changes or new features. If you looked at the code configuration, you'd notice the old helper name has been replaced with the new, officially supported one across the project's settings.

ai.title: Extract getSystemInfo into npm-app utils
ai.summary: Refactored `getSystemInfo` into `npm-app/src/utils/system-info.ts`. `project-files.ts` now imports this helper to populate `systemInfo` context. Added `npm-app` path mapping and project reference in `test/tsconfig.json`.

eli5.text: The assistant now gathers information about your computer, such as the operating system, processor count, and the command-line program it uses, in a single organized step before doing its work, instead of scattering those lookups throughout the file-handling code. If you were watching the setup process, you would see this behind-the-scenes detail collected cleanly rather than mixed into the larger file-scanning routine. Affected area: the internal file-scanning tool the assistant uses to understand your project before responding.

ai.title: PostHog event naming standardization and proxy rewrites
ai.summary: Standardized PostHog event names to dot-notation categories (e.g., `home.cta_clicked`, `subscription.payment_completed`) and added Next.js rewrites to proxy PostHog ingest traffic. Updated `web/next.config.mjs` with `/ingest` routes and `skipTrailingSlashRedirect`. Refactored tracking calls in `web/src/app/page.tsx`, `web/src/app/payment-success/page.tsx`, `web/src/components/InteractiveTerminalDemo.tsx`, and `web/src/components/CookieConsentCard.tsx` to match new schema. Removed theme context from analytics events and added client-side consent tracking.

eli5.text: The website now sends analytics events to PostHog through a proxy, so visitors' browsers route tracking data through the site's own domain instead of hitting PostHog's servers directly. Event names were also standardized to a consistent format (like 'subscription.payment_completed' instead of 'clicked "Try For Free" button'), and the team stopped sending irrelevant data like UI theme preferences while adding consent tracking so they can measure how many visitors decline analytics. This is internal housekeeping for the product team's analytics dashboard, no changes that visitors would notice in the site's appearance or behavior.

ai.title: Upgrade tree-sitter to 0.22.4
ai.summary: Bumped tree-sitter from 0.21.1 to 0.22.4 in packages/code-map/package.json. Updates core parsing dependency for code mapping functionality. Scope limited to code-map package dependencies.

eli5.text: The code-mapping tool got a small behind-the-scenes upgrade to the part of its brain that reads and understands code written in languages like C, C++, and C#. Instead of noticing any new feature or faster performance, you will simply see that the tool can now work with a slightly newer version of that reading system, which the team swapped in to keep everything running smoothly. This is purely housekeeping to keep the tool's internal parts up to date.

ai.title: Fix web crash on subscription confirm page
ai.summary: Moved `posthog` import and reordered `useUpgradeSubscription` hook initialization in `web/src/app/subscription/confirm/page.tsx`. Hook now initializes after `currentPlan` data is available, preventing undefined access. Scope limited to web subscription confirmation flow.

eli5.text: The subscription confirmation page no longer crashes when you try to upgrade your plan. You might have seen the page freeze or go blank right after selecting a new plan; that was caused by a step that ran before your current plan details were ready, and the order has been fixed so the necessary data loads first. Only the web subscription confirmation flow was affected, and the fix is live as of today.
